page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The system includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphics processing is handled by two AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPUs with a total of 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core results falling into the bottom 10%. However, multi-core capabilities are more competitive, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores all placing in the middle 50% average tier. Memory performance is a notable strength, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top 25% (strong tier), while memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks remain in the average tier.

The instance exhibits average performance for standard workloads like Redis SET operations (29.35 million operations/sec) and static web serving (11.8 GB/sec). For machine learning, LLM inference speeds for small (135M) and medium (7B) models are average, but drop to the bottom 25% for large (70B) models. The lack of AVX-512 and AMX instructions limits certain vector and matrix acceleration capabilities. This hardware configuration is suited for graphics-intensive applications, remote workstations, game streaming, and moderate database or multi-threaded processing tasks that benefit from local NVMe storage and dual AMD GPUs.
description: Amazon Web Services g4ad.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance designed for graphics-intensive workloads. It features 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.0 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory and a 1200 GB local NVMe SSD. Graphics acceleration is delivered via two AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPUs with 16 GB of total VRAM. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits a poor single-core CPU performance profile, falling into the bottom 10%, but achieves average multi-core and memory bandwidth results, alongside a strong Passmark memory score in the top 25%. Lacking AVX-512 support, it is less suited for heavy vector math but performs reliably for moderate LLM inference and multi-threaded tasks. This instance is optimized for graphics rendering, game streaming, and database workloads requiring local high-speed storage.
